content: R1: Actual enum-prose GB18466 3.1-3.4 exits 1 because citations are not bound. Wanted 9.9.9 exits 0 with zero items and complete, borrowing a reading-layer warning to bypass the contract. Bind and re-read citations, check missing requested targets, and decide answer coverage only after extraction.

R2: row_origins uses indices after removing headers, so all 13 real GB8978 row citations point to the previous raw grid row. Preserve original coordinates across header/footnote removal; independently re-read and compare every cited row. allow_partial with a missing first fragment also raises IndexError due to compressed metadata.

R3: requires_span chooses the first numbered clause without accepting the requested subrange. A unit containing 7.1, 7.5 and 7.6 returns 7.1 for the requested 7.5 scope and complete. Pass explicit request boundaries, preserve source offsets, and reject unprovable spans.

R4: table enumeration has no final source/active guard; an isolated production-entry replay counts only one guard call and still returns complete when the next guard would be stale. Prose needs a final check after extraction/model too. Document queries also ignore the requested workspace and never check the live source.

R5: A fabricated parking-lot item quoting the real clinic/ward phrase is marked citation_verified=True with no error. Substring existence proves the quote exists, not support for the item. Validate task-specific item support or leave the claim unverified and degraded.

R6: Arbitrary warnings containing extraction/items permit empty complete, and citation keys are checked only for presence. Require valid matching identities/source versions/locators and distinguish read completion from verified answer completion; prose source_snapshot_id is currently empty.

R7: The file is one formatted JSON object containing five runs plus one paragraph extraction, not 11 JSONL enumeration records. Raw model request/response is absent; current CLI/prose formatting checks fail. Generate evidence from supported entry points and describe the actual checks and records.
